subject: Combine results from separate parboot() calls that were run in parallel

messages.author: d640f02d29e7de63
messages.subject: Combine results from separate parboot() calls that were run in parallel
parts:
Hello,

I fit a model with gmultmix() and attempted to validate it with Nmix.gof.test(). One validation run of 1000 iterations took four hours, and I have several dozen models to validate (ideally with 5000 iterations each). So I am considering parallelization, possibly on an Amazon computer with 40 cores. To begin learning about this, I adapted the useful example provided by Richard here:

https://groups.google.com/d/msg/unmarked/txp1UeptjgM/bYHTPiUN55kJ

I ran the code on my own computer, which has two cores, and found that with two cores I can run 1000 iterations in half the time. So far so good.

However, the results are contained in a list, with each list element containing test results based on 500 iterations. I'd like to combine these, to be able to interpret the test results as of they were based on 1000 iterations.

This is basically the same question asked by "MP" at the end of the conversation linked above.

Many thanks for any advice or suggestions!

Mark B.
Ph.D. Candidate
University of Saskatchewan

messages.subject: Re: Combine results from separate parboot() calls that were run in parallel
parts:
Friends,

After a few simulations, I think I've determined that multiple p-values corresponding to the same test (e.g., SSE) that were obtained from separate parboot() runs  can simply be averaged to produce a "combined p-value", so long as the number of iterations is held constant across parboot() runs. Does this make sense?

Thanks, Mark

messages.author: 527d9b3ec7deff2d
messages.subject: Re: Combine results from separate parboot() calls that were run in parallel
parts:
Hi Mark, I'm pasting the source code used to generate the summary for a parboot object below.  It should be pretty straightforward to combine the matrices of t.star fit values across the separate runs and calculate the necessary statistics using this:

    t.star <- obj...@t.star
    t0 <- object@t0
    nsim <- nrow(t.star)
    biasMat <- pMat <- matrix(NA, nsim, length(t0))
    for(i in 1:nsim) {
        biasMat[i,] <- t0 - t.star[i,]
        pMat[i,] <- abs(t.star[i,] - 1) > abs(t0 - 1)
        }
    bias <- colMeans(biasMat)
    bias.se <- apply(biasMat, 2, sd)
    p.val <- colSums(pMat) / (1 + nsim)
    stats <- data.frame("t0" = t0, "mean(t0 - t_B)" = bias,
        "StdDev(t0 - t_B)" = bias.se, "Pr(t_B > t0)" = p.val,
        check.names = FALSE)

parts:
Many thanks to Dan for suggesting that I combine my two t.star matrices (resulting from separate parboot runs) into a new, single t.star matrix, on which the unmarked source code (which Dan provided) can be run, to produce combined validation statistics and p-values.

Here's the code Dan helped me with. Only the first two lines, and the last one, are new; the rest is unmarked source code...

t.star <- rbind(sims[[1]]@t.star,sims[[2]]@t.star) #sims is the name of a list containing two parboot objects
t0 <- sims[[1]]@t0 #OR sims[[2]]@t0 because they're the same

nsim <- nrow(t.star)
biasMat <- pMat <- matrix(NA, nsim, length(t0))
for(i in 1:nsim) {
  biasMat[i,] <- t0 - t.star[i,]
  pMat[i,] <- abs(t.star[i,] - 1) > abs(t0 - 1)
}
bias <- colMeans(biasMat)
bias.se <- apply(biasMat, 2, sd)
p.val <- colSums(pMat) / (1 + nsim)
stats <- data.frame("t0" = t0, "mean(t0 - t_B)" = bias,
                    "StdDev(t0 - t_B)" = bias.se, "Pr(t_B > t0)" = p.val,
                    check.names = FALSE)

stats #inspect combined stats

Thanks again to Dan for taking the time to help.
